nodes.title: server/signals/backstop.js safetyBackstop(): abstain-only pattern check for the 4 distress shapes the floor predicate missed in ES-3 (mujhe marna hai, rahun ya na rahun, kisi ko farak nahi padta main hoon ya nahi, I hate my life + Devanagari forms). A hit makes step() return ABSTAIN; it never routes or answers. Routing stays W2-I's (scanSafety). Reverse when scanSafety covers these shapes and ES-3 floor misses = 0 (then keep it as defence in depth or delete).

After any safety turn the signal layer withholds playful licences (childWin child_joke, choiceDue) for 3 child turns (SignalSession.safetyHold). RELATIONAL-OS owns the check-in after distress. Reverse if E1 coders find the hold suppresses a wanted LAUGH-WITH after a false-alarm safety turn more often than 1 in 10.

SL-4 over the D7 rule table: acoustic drift G3 can fire the composite break offer only alongside a T worsening (G4 > 0); G3 alone never fires it. The spec's D7 row (G4 >= 0.25 OR G3 sustained) contradicted SL-4/G-SIG-COST. Reverse only if SG-M15 shows G3 adds break precision when G4 <= 0.

A graded correct/partial answer, or any graded answer on a choice_spoken item, is never a non-answer; an empty transcript over >= 600 ms of detected speech is an STT miss, not a non-answer. Before: a shy child's three correct 'haan'/'nahi' fired choiceDue at turn 3, and three STT misses did the same. Reverse if E1 shows disengaged children's graded minimal answers are missed by choiceDue more than 30% of runs.

Bare 'break' / 'rest' / 'baad mein' / 'aaram' / 'slow' / 'dheere' as meta-request lexicon entries: they are lesson content ('24 ko break karo 20 aur 4 mein', 'the rest is half', 'aaram se ho jayega', 'pehle guna, baad mein jod', 'kachhua dheere chalta hai') and fired breakDue(child_said) / paceDown on 6/6 probe answers. Replaced by request-shaped phrases; ES-1 child_said break recall unchanged (0.870), paceDown recall 0.624 -> 0.710.

Treating 'na'/'न' within 2 tokens AFTER a lexicon hit as negation: in Hinglish it is the tag particle ('thoda dheere bolo na', 'break do na'), so real requests were silently dropped. 'na' now negates only pre-verbally ('na karo'). Part of the paceDown recall gain 0.624 -> 0.710 on ES-1.

Signals verify re-run (node evals/signals/run.mjs, 2026-10-04, this container): build numbers reproduced exactly before fixes (ES-1 8357 turns, ES-3 284/300 pipeline, ES-4 precisions, ES-5 p99 0.69 ms max 5.0 ms). After fixes: ES-1 unchanged except paceDown recall 0.624 -> 0.710 (precision 1.0); guardrails 0 violations; ES-3 frame pass 300/300 but FLOOR predicate misses still 16 turns / 4 distinct (now counted from scanSafety directly); backstop 16/16 on those, 0 false hits on 9,171 non-distress synthetic turns (ES-1 8357 + ES-3 non-a 220 + ES-4 594; patterns written by the reviewer after seeing the misses, so held-out recall is unknown); ES-5 p50 0.48 ms p99 0.90 ms max 6.1 ms (n=10,000); 5,000-token pathological transcript 13.5 ms -> 1.2 ms after a 1,200-char cap. 'AUC' in the summary is balanced accuracy (TPR+TNR)/2 on boolean rules, not a ranking AUC.

W2-I: add the four ES-3 shapes (see sig-review-safety-backstop) to server/director/safety.js scanSafety so the floor routes them (helplines, safeguard hand-off). Until then the signal layer only abstains; the child gets no floor response unless the production classifier catches them (not run offline).
